subject: Hosted API quickstart, endpoints & rate limits — decision checklist
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Brijesh Singh <brijesh@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API quickstart, endpoints & rate limits — decision checklist

Hi Brijesh —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a small checklist so we can land on the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

- Demo notes: you liked the low-latency warm KV caching and the canary fallback behavior.
- Clarifying question: is StellarPay comfortable starting on Hosted for an evaluation (48–72h trial with production-like traffic) or do procurement/security require Dedicated/Private from day one?

To help us recommend the right onramp, can you confirm the following by end of week?
1) Expected peak requests/sec and average sequence length (tokens) during peak.
2) Latency SLO target (P50/P95) and max allowed cold-starts per minute.
3) Any hard requirements on data residency / VPC/HSM / audit log forwarding.
4) Procurement timeline and whether you will insist on Reserved Capacity or accept a Hosted trial before committing.

What we can deliver quickly if you opt for Hosted evaluation:
- Short-lived trial endpoints (/v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings) mapped to your test workspace.
- Default rate caps: 200 requests/sec per endpoint (soft), token-based throttles (configurable).
- Burst policy: automatic short-term bursting up to 2x for demos (subject to account limits).

I attached a one-page ops checklist that outlines the quickstart steps and the information we need to provision the trial. Once you confirm the traffic profile and security constraints we’ll do a short preflight and spin up the trial.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-ops-checklist.pdf (ops checklist)

Proposed next steps:
- Brijesh: confirm items 1–4 above by Apr 22.
- Redwood (Aditya & team): prep Hosted trial config and SLA addendum for procurement review.
- Schedule a 30-min preflight on Apr 22 if that works for your infra lead.

Thanks — look forward to moving fast on this.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
https://redwood.ai
From: Brijesh Singh <brijesh@stellarpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart, endpoints & rate limits — decision checklist

Kimberly —

Appreciate the recap and the checklist. Short answers to help you size things:
- Peak profile: ~120 requests/sec at peak (checkout burst windows), median sequence ~55–70 tokens, average payload small (~600 bytes).
- Latency SLO: target P50 < 200ms, P95 < 600ms. For checkout flows we prefer p99 as low as possible but can tolerate 1–2% higher during deploys.
- Security: StellarPay is SOC 2 Type II and requires evidence of SOC controls; data residency restricted to US regions only; we will require audit log forwarding to our Splunk instance or S3 export.
- Procurement: our procurement team prefers Reserved Capacity for production, but the engineering team is OK evaluating Hosted for a 2–4 week pilot if logs/anonymization and an SLA addendum are provided.

So Hosted trial is acceptable to validate latency and integration. The procurement team will still push for Dedicated if the cost model and SLA are favorable. I’ve looped procurement: procurement@stellarpay.com — they may ask for pricing math and a draft SLA.

Also: can you confirm the endpoints and the effective rate limits in tokens/sec? We’ll need that to build a realistic load generator.

Thanks,
Brijesh
Head of Integrations, StellarPay
brijesh@stellarpay.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart, endpoints & rate limits — decision checklist

Kimberly / Sean —

Adding a technical summary that we can send to Brijesh/procurement to make the Hosted trial deterministic. I included the SLA addendum draft as an attachment for procurement to review.

Key trial deliverables (Hosted):
- Endpoints: /v1/generate (batch & streaming), /v1/chat (stateful chat with KV cache), /v1/embeddings. We will provision separate test API keys and a dedicated test workspace.
- Default rate caps (initial): 200 reqs/sec per endpoint (soft limit), 1,200,000 tokens/min account-wide (configurable).
- Burst behavior: short-lived bursts allowed up to 2x the soft limit for 60s windows; sustained increases require reserved capacity commit.
- Concurrency guidance: for your sequence lengths (~60 tokens) we recommend initial concurrency pool of 50 workers to meet P50 <200ms in Hosted; we can tune after pilot telemetry.
- Logging & exports: we support audit log streaming to S3 or Splunk (encrypted in transit), and we can provide redacted request logs that meet SOC2 evidence requirements.

Cost & timelines:
- Hosted pilot: typically 48–72h to provision with full telemetry, 1–2 business days if no special VPC/HSM integration required.
- Dedicated: 2–4 weeks lead time for reserved GPU pool provisioning and capacity sizing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): multi-week to months depending on network approvals; recommended only if procurement requires it.

Attachments: redwood-sla-addendum-draft.docx (SLA addendum for procurement review)

Action for external: we should send Brijesh a short technical bullet list (endpoints + effective rate caps + logging options) and the SLA draft. If procurement accepts the SLA addendum, we can run the Hosted pilot while they finalize Reserved Capacity negotiations.

I’ll draft a concise note for Brijesh.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Brijesh Singh <brijesh@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, procurement@stellarpay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart, endpoints & rate limits — decision checklist

Brijesh / procurement —

Thanks — summarizing and proposing concrete next steps so we can move to a Hosted pilot while procurement reviews a Reserved Capacity option:

Summary of what Redwood will provide for the Hosted evaluation:
- Test endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings (separate test API keys and workspace).
- Rate caps: soft 200 reqs/sec per endpoint, account-wide 1,200,000 tokens/min; burst allowance up to 2x for short windows.
- Telemetry: audit log streaming to S3 or Splunk; request log redaction options for SOC2 evidence.
- Timeline: we can provision the trial within 48–72 hours once you confirm the traffic profile and grant access for log export.
- SLA addendum: attached draft for your procurement team to review; we can tighten SLA terms for Reserved Capacity if you move to Dedicated.

Action items / owners:
- Brijesh: confirm peak requests/sec and any additional security constraints (due Apr 25).
- Procurement@stellarpay.com: review attached SLA draft and share procurement timeline/required redlines.
- Redwood (Aditya): provision trial endpoints & API keys after Brijesh confirms traffic profile; prepare DocuSign for SLA addendum.
- Kimberly: schedule a 30-min preflight meeting Apr 22 to validate integration points (I’ll send calendar invite).

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-ops-checklist.pdf; redwood-sla-addendum-draft.docx

If procurement prefers to skip Hosted and go directly to Dedicated we can provide pricing math and committed capacity timelines (2–4 weeks). Otherwise, running the Hosted pilot in parallel gives your engineers the fastest way to validate latency and integration.

Thanks — I’ll share the calendar invite and the short technical bullet list (endpoints + effective rate caps) in a separate note.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
